problem: Productionize the validated Hybrid seed/restoration topology so players can buy and visibly plant owned Daisy/Clover/Lavender species during recovery without changing authored native campaign identities, creating a repeat aesthetic tax, breaking progression, or adding a modal inventory/input owner; the flow must persist through save v3 and work on desktop and touch.

decision.rationale: Keep the three native campaign patches authored and progression-bearing while adding two clearly bounded YOUR PLOT spaces that never contribute to campaign completion. Seed ownership is a one-time Honey sink (15/18/22), owned-species replant is free, and save v3 stores seed ownership/player plants separately from native campaign completion. Exact-head Test/data and Chromium proof show 120/120 purchase priorities remain no-grind, real desktop/touch planting works, free replant does not mutate campaign state, and ownership/customization survives reload.

anti_pattern.lesson: Do not maximize customization freedom by allowing P5 planting to erase the authored identity or progression meaning of incomplete native campaign patches.

Persistence remains behind the protected versioned storage service. Seed ownership/player plants are independent domain state and therefore use an explicit v2-to-v3 migration rather than being inferred from campaign completion.

findings: The Hybrid roles are visually separated enough for the autonomous P5 milestone: chosen flowers live only inside bounded YOUR PLOT spaces, while native campaign patches retain their authored flower/progression role; locked player plots explicitly defer to native restoration.
Seed choice is materially visible: the same player plot changes from empty/offer to Daisy, Clover and back to Daisy in retained frames without changing native completion.
The flow remains low-friction on desktop and touch: one contextual SPACE / TAP interaction executes purchase/plant/replant, with no seed modal or inventory input owner.
